title: Arnav Talukder Is Building Ralli to Help Pickleball Players Find Their Community
summary: Arnav Talukder Is Building Ralli to Help Pickleball Players Find Their Community
body_markdown:
Pickleball has quickly become one of the[fastest-growing sports in America](https://www.forbes.com/sites/jefffromm/2026/02/12/how-pickleball-became-americas-fastest-growing-sport-even-among-gen-z/) , with over[2,300 courts opened in 2025 alone](https://usapickleball.org/about/annual-growth-report/) . Part of the reason for the emerging sport’s rapid growth is its accessibility. Whether you’re a college student or a senior citizen, you can pick up a paddle and play.


But the broad range of pickleball players also makes it difficult to find the right people to play with. While some players are looking for a leisurely social activity, others want competitive matches that will challenge their ability.


After health challenges sidelined him from sports for years,[Arnav Talukder](https://www.linkedin.com/in/arnav-talukder/) fell in love with pickleball as it made it possible for him to re-enter competitive sports at his own pace. But he quickly realized that to have fun and improve, he needed to be playing with people his own age and skill level. So he set out to build[Ralli](https://dinkralli.com/) , a social matchmaking platform that brings pickleball players together in small, curated groups.


## Introducing Ralli: Social Matchmaking for Pickleball


Ralli was built around a simple insight, Arnav explains: “Anyone can play pickleball, but not everyone is at the same step in their journey.” Yet open play events pack as many as 50 people onto four courts and force players to wait 20–30 minutes for a game, only to be matched with someone at a different skill level. Leagues offer another way to play, but many players view them as too competitive.


Ralli is taking a different approach. By organizing players into groups of four to six based on skill level, interests, personalities, and the type of experience they're looking for, the platform enables players to enjoy the game on their own terms and build genuine connections both on and off the court. Instead of the lottery of open play, players skip the long waits and mismatched games, and are more likely to meet people they actually click with.


## Arnav’s Journey to Ralli


Growing up in Michigan, Arnav developed a love for competitive sports from an early age, playing baseball, golf, and tennis throughout the year. In eighth grade, however, he developed unexpected brain inflammation that led to him being in a coma and staying in the hospital for six months.


Arnav recovered, but the extended period of inactivity caused severe muscle atrophy, effectively removing him from competitive sports for years to come. “I couldn’t really get back to sports for years. Even playing for fun was a struggle,” Arnav says. “All through high school, and even in college, there were times when my friends had to drop me off at my dorm room door because I was too weak to walk across the dorms.”


It wasn’t until last year that Arnav found his way back to sports, when he decided to give pickleball a try and quickly fell in love with it. “You don’t have to be fast, and everyone plays at their own pace. And it’s super social.”


Just as he picked up pickleball, Arnav was at a crossroads in his professional life. He had been working in tax and accounting, but was considering a career change and weighing graduate school offers from schools like Duke, USC and Georgetown.


When he recognized the need to connect pickleball players specifically around their age and skill level, he began floating the idea of a pickleball matchmaking platform around his local courts. Within days, dozens of players said they’d be interested, and he knew the opportunity was there.


Arnav built the initial MVP himself and was accepted to UCLA’s accelerator for early-stage startups from UCLA alumni. He soon brought friend and fellow pickleball player, Mario, onto the team to help further develop the platform. Validated by his alma mater’s belief in the idea and early user testing, Arnav decided to pass on his graduate school opportunities, quit his job, and go full-time working on Ralli.


After launching on July 4th, 2026, Ralli reached 50 users in just two weeks and has already grown to over 130 users, partnering with three courts in the Los Angeles area. Arnav is currently focused on establishing Ralli in Southern California before launching in other regions in the near future. In the long run, Arnav aims to expand beyond pickleball and develop Ralli into a platform that helps people find their communities through sports broadly.


## Arnav’s Advice for Fellow Founders


Arnav admits that at the beginning of this year, he never would have guessed that he’d be running his own startup with over 100 users and early revenue by the end of the year. But by recognizing a problem he was facing, and building in a space that he’s passionate about, he’s been able to exceed his wildest expectations. If you’re considering starting a business, “just take the leap and try it out,” he says, because you never know where it may lead.


And as you’re getting started, talk to anyone and everyone, Arnav says. “A lot of our good contacts and growth channels have actually come from random meetings with someone I just met at a pickleball facility, or even in passing. Anyone and everyone could be of help.”


To learn more about Arnav’s journey building Ralli, you can[follow him on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/arnav-talukder/) and visit[dinkralli.com](http://dinkralli.com/) .
